title: Prove selected BIT packet integration and live-row layout
body:
I prove a selected BIT integration lemma over GL64(Z/q^w): complete local words preserve their COPY/ERASE guards and hosted endpoints when the caller batches all high matrices for one low cover class. I also give an explicit live-row layout that preserves the selected child-volume denominator and supplies complete descendant stock.

The packet distinction matters. Two owners can differ at each fixed matrix while their full high packets coincide. I prove low-packet separation for the selected helper completions and add an exact alias countermodel. I also reject transpose and reorthogonalization shortcuts that pass modulo 3 but fail over Z/9.

Evidence:

- 4,668 split-rank cases, 14,370 weighted transports and 181,056 selected same-family owner pairs.
- A sequential restricted-fibre XOR over all 3,888 GL2(Z/9) rows, moving 198,288 payload bits while preserving the other 47 low packets.
- An explicit mixed-radix layout with `lcm(28416,28425)`, complete child stock and the exact live denominator `28416*|GL64(Fq)|`.
- Registered Python 3.12 replay passed normally and with `-O`; source pins and deterministic receipt comparison passed.

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-local-ring-sweeps
```

I reuse alephnan's [PR1627](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1627) literal audit and whole-call proof, and credit eumemic's [PR490](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/490) for the generic GL argument. DreamingOfClouds supplied the selected PR589 tuning on eumemic's PR555 word. The package records exact predecessor heads, including the recent routing, stock, weighted-child and fallback work. I also credit commdata2338's concurrent [PR2188](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2188) mixed diagonal-pair descriptor and retain its remaining shear/physical integration question.

Scope: written proof and finite certificates, conditional on completed address callees and their work/restoration contracts. Recursive scratch allocation, the selected finite routing invoice and outer transfer remain open. I claim no new exponent or complete multiplication theorem.

Coordination: [Discussion2179](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2179). I started from canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision4. I contributed as `jmbarrancoml` with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review claimed.
